title: Citizens Public Safety Review and Appeal Board
content: Provides independent community oversight of the Kalamazoo Department of Public Safety. Hears appeals of complaint investigations conducted by the Office of Professional Standards and advises the City Manager on policies, procedures, and community relations.

title: Citizens Public Safety Review and Appeal Board — About & Mission
content: The Citizens Public Safety Review and Appeal Board (CPSRAB) provides an opportunity for community members to participate in the oversight of the Kalamazoo Department of Public Safety (KDPS). Established by the City Manager's Office, the Board receives citizen input on appeals filed after KDPS complaint investigations and can inquire into any conduct of a public safety officer in the absence of a complaint. The Board serves three primary purposes: building community trust and credibility in the public safety complaint process; providing an independent review of complaint dispositions that citizens choose to appeal; and advising the City Manager on improvements to policies, procedures, and community outreach related to the complaint process. For more information about the Board, its work, and annual reports, visit the Board's independent website: kalamazoocpsrab.org.

title: Citizens Public Safety Review and Appeal Board — Roles & Responsibilities
content: Review Receive copies of complaints (with personal information redacted) upon request. Be updated monthly on the progress of all active complaint investigations by the Office of Professional Standards. Inquire about any complaint investigation, regardless of the Chief's finding, in the absence of a formal appeal. Review the complaint reporting process and recommend improvements to the Chief and City Manager. Advisory Monitor the overall fairness of the complaint process for both citizens and public safety employees. Recommend improvements to the City Manager on policies and procedures implicated in the complaint process. Assist the Department of Public Safety in preparing community outreach materials about the complaint process. Establish subcommittees to research and address public safety and community relations issues. Reporting Prepare an annual review covering the number and types of complaints, and assess the thoroughness, accountability, and responsiveness of the complaint process. Issue reports on police/community relations, racial profiling, and other community climate concerns as needed. Community Outreach Hold meetings with community leaders and neighborhood associations at least annually. Organize public forums to discuss community climate and develop action agendas with the Public Safety Chief. Work with KDPS and community organizations to anticipate and prevent problems through data analysis and recommendations.

title: Citizens Public Safety Review and Appeal Board — Membership Requirements
content: The Board consists of up to 12 members appointed by the City Manager: up to 6 from diverse organizations representing diverse populations and up to 6 at-large members. A quorum requires 51% of active members present. Appointment All members are appointed by the City Manager. The Chair is named annually by the City Manager; the Vice Chair is recommended by the Chair and approved by the City Manager. Term Length Members serve 3-year terms, limited to 2 consecutive terms. A 1-year hiatus is required before reappointment. Residency Full-time City of Kalamazoo residents receive first priority. Non-residents with identifiable interests located in the City receive second priority. Time Commitment Approximately 5-8 hours per calendar quarter, including monthly meetings, two KDPS ride-alongs or hiring events per year, and two community outreach events per year. Disqualifiers Members may not hold political office, be a current City employee, work for another law enforcement agency, be a retired or former law enforcement officer, or be an immediate family member of any KDPS personnel. Orientation Members must attend an orientation session within their first 90 days and attend the Kalamazoo Regional Citizens Academy within the first year of service.

title: Citizens Public Safety Review and Appeal Board — How appeals work
content: Six steps run from the complaint to the final decision. Two of them are yours, and most carry a deadline. File a complaint Kalamazoo Department of Public Safety Complaints about a public safety employee are investigated by the Office of Professional Standards, which is a division inside the Kalamazoo Department of Public Safety. You can file online, by phone, in person at any station, or by mail. The investigation and the finding Office of Professional Standards The Office of Professional Standards completes its investigation within 45 days of the complaint being filed. If more time is needed, the inspector assigned to the case contacts you with an estimated completion date. The findings then go to the Chief of Public Safety for a final determination, and you receive written notice of the outcome. You are also sent a follow up evaluation form, notice of your right to appeal, and a stamped envelope addressed back to the city so you can start an appeal. File an appeal City Manager's Office If you disagree with the finding, you appeal to the City Manager's Office. Your appeal form and the response letter you received must both be received by the City Manager's Office no later than 15 business days after you received that letter, which is roughly three calendar weeks. Incomplete materials are not processed. There is only one appeal form: the city titles it the City Manager's Office Appeal Form, and the Board's own site refers to it as its appeal form. The hearing The Board After examining the appeal material, the City Manager refers the matter to the Board, and the City Manager's Office schedules a hearing within 30 business days. The hearing is held no later than 60 business days after the appeal is filed. Present at the hearing are you, a representative from the Office of Professional Standards, a representative from the City Manager's Office, and members of the Board. You may appear in person, and you choose on the appeal form whether the hearing is open to the public or closed. The Board reviews the case materials but does not hear from witnesses other than the Chief of Public Safety or the Chief's designee. The Board's recommendation The Board The Board deliberates privately and sends a written report to the City Manager no later than 15 business days after the hearing. It can recommend that the Chief's finding be upheld or changed to sustained, and it can ask in writing for further investigation. It cannot impose discipline, and it cannot recommend that discipline be imposed or increased. The City Manager decides City Manager's Office The City Manager holds final authority and may sustain or amend the response made by the Chief of Public Safety and the recommendation made by the Board. You will receive notification of the findings from the City Manager no later than 20 business days after the hearing. The City Manager's decision concludes the appeal process. What an appeal can and cannot do The Board is an outside check on an investigation carried out inside the Kalamazoo Department of Public Safety. It cannot discipline anyone. The strongest outcome an appeal can produce is a recommendation to the City Manager that the Chief of Public Safety’s finding be changed to sustained. Decisions about discipline are made separately and are not part of this process. Which findings can be appealed Whether you can appeal depends entirely on which finding the Chief of Public Safety reached. The finding is named in the written notice you received, so check that letter for the exact wording before you file. Sustained There was sufficient evidence to prove what you reported. This finding cannot be appealed. Not sustained The investigation could not prove or disprove what you reported. This finding can be appealed. Unfounded The investigation proved conclusively that the acts described did not occur. This finding can be appealed. Exonerated The actions described did occur, but were found to be justified or proper. This finding can be appealed. Misconduct not based on complaint The investigation uncovered improper job performance unrelated to what you reported. This finding can be appealed. Exceptionally cleared The complainant did not cooperate with the investigation, or did not provide enough information for it to proceed. The Board names four findings it can hear on appeal and this is not among them. Contact the Board directly if you received this finding.

title: Civil Rights Board
content: Reviews claims of discrimination brought by City residents under the Non-Discrimination and Fair Housing Ordinances, and makes recommendations for resolution after investigation by the City Manager. Also recommends ways to improve City programs and ordinances to eliminate discrimination. Established September 2020 under Chapter 18 of the Code of Ordinances.

title: Civil Rights Board — About & Mission
content: The Civil Rights Board implements the general policy and purposes set forth in Chapter 18 "Non-Discrimination" and Chapter 18A "Fair Housing" of the City of Kalamazoo Code of Ordinances. The Board was created in September 2020 following updates to Chapter 18. The Board fosters mutual understanding and respect among the people in the City, working to discourage and prevent unlawful discriminatory practices toward the protected classes described in the Ordinance. Board meetings are conducted under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, and Board records are available to the public under the Michigan Freedom of Information Act.

title: Civil Rights Board — Roles & Responsibilities
content: Review Review claims of discrimination brought by City residents and make recommendations for resolution, following investigation of the claim by the City Manager or the City Manager's designee. Review and analyze conditions, practices, attitudes, policies and other factors within Kalamazoo that contribute to discriminatory impact and further inequities. Evaluate the impact of antidiscrimination efforts. Advisory Make recommendations to the City Commission and City Manager on ways to improve City programs and ordinances to eliminate discrimination. Make recommendations on ways to remove the effects of past discrimination. Establish bylaws and procedural rules for its meetings, subject to approval by the City Commission. Reporting Provide an annual report to the City Commission on complaints received and actions taken. Under the bylaws, the Chairperson sees that the annual report is submitted by February 1 each year. Community Outreach Foster mutual understanding and respect among the people in the City, and discourage and prevent unlawful discriminatory practices toward the protected classes described in the Ordinance. Engage in public awareness activities so residents are informed of local protections and the role of the Board. Engage with federal, state and local agencies to assist in addressing issues of discrimination in the City. The Board reviews claims and makes recommendations. Investigation of a claim is carried out by the City Manager or the City Manager's designee, not by the Board.

title: Civil Rights Board — Membership Requirements
content: The Board consists of 9 members: 7 voting members and 2 ex-officio members who have no vote but may otherwise fully participate in any meeting. Appointment Voting members are appointed by the Mayor and approved by the City Commission. Expertise Required Members must be able to demonstrate experience in civil rights, public accommodation, employment, disability or housing law. Residency Members shall be residents of the City, reflecting and representing the diversity of the Kalamazoo community. Up to 2 members may be non-residents when there is a valid reason, such as working in the City or holding special expertise needed to carry out the Board's duties. Ex-Officio Members One City Commissioner, and one City officer or employee recommended by the City Manager who is neither a City Commissioner nor the City Manager. Both are appointed by the Mayor and approved by the City Commission. Term Length Three years. Members may serve up to two consecutive terms. A member whose term has expired may continue to serve until a successor is appointed. Attendance A member absent for 3 consecutive meetings, or for more than 50% of regular meetings over a six-month period, is considered to have resigned and the seat is deemed vacant. Quorum Five members. Ex-officio members count toward establishing a quorum.

title: Civil Rights Board — How complaints work
content: Five steps run from the complaint to the Board's recommendation. The first two are yours, and the complaint carries a deadline. Gather your information You Before filing, collect what happened and when, and the person or organization the complaint is about. It also helps to note whether you have already referred the complaint elsewhere, such as the Fair Housing Center of Southwest Michigan or the Michigan Department of Civil Rights. File the complaint You File online, or bring the paper form to City Hall during business hours, or mail it to the City Manager's Office at 241 W South Street. The incident must have happened inside Kalamazoo city limits and within the last 91 days, or it cannot be investigated. Complaints that fall outside the City's ordinance are referred to the appropriate authority. The City confirms receipt City staff A member of the City's team follows up within three business days to confirm your complaint was received. If you filed online, you are also notified once the appropriate staff have reviewed it whether it will be investigated. The investigation City staff, not the Board The complaint is investigated by City staff with relevant knowledge and experience, under the City Manager or the City Manager's designee. The Board does not investigate. The results of the investigation are shared with the Board. The Board's recommendation The Board The Board reviews the claim and the investigation results. If the ordinance was violated, the Board makes a recommendation to the City Manager on how it should be addressed. The Board recommends; it does not decide or enforce. Before you file The incident must have happened within Kalamazoo city limits. Complaints more than 91 days after the incident cannot be investigated. Complaints become public information and may be discussed by the Civil Rights Board or released under a Freedom of Information Act request. The City says it uses discretion when responding. Local protections go beyond state and federal law, covering source of income, status as a survivor of domestic violence, and prior arrest or conviction record.

title: Zoning Board of Appeals
content: Hears requests for variances from the Zoning Ordinance, provides interpretations of the Ordinance, and hears appeals of administrative zoning decisions made by the City Planner or another administrative official. Decisions are final at the City level and can only be appealed to the Circuit Court.

title: Zoning Board of Appeals — About & Mission
content: The Zoning Board of Appeals hears requests for variances from the Zoning Ordinance, provides interpretations of the Ordinance, and hears appeals of administrative zoning decisions made by the City Planner or another administrative official. The Board was established by the City of Kalamazoo as authorized by the Michigan Zoning Enabling Act, MCL § 125.3101 et seq., under § 11.3 of Appendix A, the City of Kalamazoo Zoning Ordinance. Its stated purpose is to hear and decide questions that arise in the administration of the Zoning Ordinance. Board meetings follow Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised, though the Chair may adjust procedure to suit the needs of the Board. The Board's decision is the end of the process at the City level. An appeal of a Zoning Board of Appeals decision must be filed with the Circuit Court within 30 days after the Board makes its decision in writing, or within 21 days after the Board approves the minutes of the meeting.

title: Zoning Board of Appeals — Roles & Responsibilities
content: Review Review, hear, consider and approve, approve with conditions or disapprove variances. Hear, review, consider, and affirm, partly affirm, modify or reverse any order, decision, determination or interpretation of the City Planner or any other city administrative official made under the Zoning Ordinance. Review, hear, consider and approve, approve with conditions or disapprove a change from one nonconforming use to another nonconforming use. Requests the Board Hears Dimensional variance: relief from physical or dimensional standards that apply to a lot or structure. Use variance: relief from standards that apply to how a lot or structure is used. Administrative appeal: relief from a zoning decision made by Community Planning and Economic Development staff. Interpretation of the Ordinance: a request to confirm the precise meaning of the ordinance text. Temporary use approval: approval of a temporary use lasting more than 30 days. Natural features protection: relief from standards that apply to protected natural areas. How Decisions Are Made After hearing an appeal, the Board makes a finding of fact: the facts and circumstances it relied on, based on the evidence presented to it. To reverse or modify a decision, the Board needs competent, material and substantial evidence on the record that the decision failed to comply with the Zoning Ordinance, state law, or the federal or state constitution, and a concurring vote of the majority of Board members. The Board may impose conditions ensuring the requirements and purposes of the Zoning Ordinance are met on any affirmative decision. If the Board does not decide on the day of the hearing after all evidence is presented, it must decide by the next regularly scheduled meeting. Unless the Board specifies otherwise, a granted variance becomes null and void if it is not exercised within one year of being granted. The Board decides these requests rather than recommending them onward. City staff review applications and advise the Board, but the vote to grant or deny is the Board's.

title: Zoning Board of Appeals — Membership Requirements
content: The Board consists of eight members: six regular members and two alternate members. Appointment Members are appointed by the City Commission. Under the bylaws, appointments follow a recommendation from the Board itself. Eligibility Members must be residents of the City of Kalamazoo and serve without compensation. No member of the City Commission and no City employee may serve on the Board. Representation In recommending members, the Board aims for a membership that represents a cross-section of the community by gender, race and neighborhood, that includes experience or interest in the subjects routinely before the Board, and that reflects several points of view. Term Length Three years. Members may not serve more than two consecutive terms, not counting time spent filling the unexpired term of a former member. Vacancies A vacancy is filled for the remaining term using the same procedure as an original appointment. Absences A member absent for more than 50% of regular meetings over a six-month period is considered to have resigned. The Board then recommends someone to fill the remaining term, subject to City Commission approval. Alternate Members There is a first and a second alternate; the alternate with the most seniority is the first alternate. Alternates may take part in all deliberations but do not vote unless a regular member cannot vote because of absence or a conflict of interest. The first alternate has priority to replace the first regular member unable to vote, and the second alternate replaces the second. Quorum Four members, regular or alternate. No meeting may be called to order and no business transacted without them. If no quorum is present, the meeting is rescheduled to the next regularly scheduled meeting. Officers A Chair, Vice-Chair and Secretary, elected by the Board at its Annual Meeting, which is the first regular meeting in February. Officers serve one-year terms and may be re-elected. A staff employee of the Community Development and Planning Department serves as Recording Secretary and has no vote.

title: Zoning Board of Appeals — How a request reaches the Board
content: Two routes lead to the same hearing. Five of the six request types are applications for permission, and one, an appeal of an administrative decision, is a challenge to a decision already made. They diverge at the start and converge at the hearing. Identify which route you are on You Applications for permission cover dimensional variances, use variances, ordinance interpretations, temporary use approvals, and natural features protection. An administrative appeal is different: it challenges an order, decision, determination or interpretation already made by the City Planner or another city official, and it must be made in writing within 30 days of the date of that decision. The application route has no equivalent 30-day clock, only the four-week filing deadline in step 3. Both routes carry a filing fee, listed below. Start the request You Applying for permission: schedule a pre-application meeting with the Zoning Administrator to confirm an application is needed and to go over the timeline, the required forms, and what you must do to notify neighbors. Contact Pete Eldridge at (269) 337-8806 or eldridgep@kalamazoocity.org. Appealing a decision: put the appeal in writing within 30 days. The City Planner or the official whose decision is being appealed then transmits the appeal and all related papers, documents and materials to the Board. File it You Applying for permission: complete the application form and the review sheet matching your request type, with supporting documents such as a site sketch, plan, photographs or letters of support. File online, or by mail or in person at Community Planning and Economic Development, 150 E. Crosstown Parkway, Suite B. Submit four weeks before the meeting you want to be heard at. A filing fee applies; the amount depends on the request type and is listed below. Appealing a decision: the written appeal is the filing, and the record assembled by the City Planner goes to the Board with it. Notice and scheduling You and the City The City mails notice of the public hearing to every property owner within 300 feet, giving the address, the type of request, and the date, time and location. Applicants should also contact the neighborhood association, neighbors and nearby property owners, because the Board will ask about that outreach at the hearing. An appeal is scheduled for the next regularly scheduled meeting that satisfies the written notice requirements of the Zoning Ordinance. The hearing and the decision You and the Board Both routes end here. You or a representative must attend, and you have ten minutes to explain the request. On an appeal, the city staff whose decision is being challenged appear in person to present information when work has already started. The Board makes a finding of fact based on the evidence presented, then votes. To reverse or modify a decision it needs competent, material and substantial evidence that the decision failed to comply with the Zoning Ordinance, state law, or the federal or state constitution, and a concurring vote of the majority of Board members. If it does not decide on the day of the hearing, it must decide by the next regularly scheduled meeting. Fees Use variance: $390. Dimensional variance: $312. Appeal of an administrative decision: $312. Ordinance interpretation: $286. Temporary use: $156. Amounts are from the City's 2026 CPED Fee Schedule and are set annually. Deadlines An appeal of a decision by the City Planner or another city official must be made in writing within 30 days of the date of that decision. Applications for permission are due four weeks before the meeting you want to be heard at. A granted variance becomes null and void if it is not exercised within one year, unless the Board specifies otherwise. A decision by the Board can only be appealed to the Circuit Court, within 30 days after the written decision or 21 days after the minutes are approved. At the hearing Meetings are held the second Thursday of each month at 7 p.m. in City Hall. You or a representative must attend, and you have ten minutes to present. Variances granted by the Board apply to the site plan and documents submitted at the hearing.
